name: get_annotations
description: Read the planning annotations. Without id: a compact survey of every zone (number, tag, colour, id, area, bounds, pieces, touching zones), overlaps, how much open buildable ground the zones cover, circulation (entrance zones and routes) and whether it reaches the fixed landmarks, the largest unplanned ground, and every chip, route and measure. With id: that one annotation in full, its cells included. These are planning ink, not terrain or placed objects. Unfinished user drafts are separate and cannot be edited by these tools.

name: set_annotation
description: Create a planning annotation, or update the supplied id. Updates preserve omitted fields and cannot change kind. A zone takes shapes (preferred) or explicit cells. Shapes are unioned in order and a shape with cut subtracts: rect and ellipse fill the inclusive box x1,y1,x2,y2; ring is that ellipse's outline of the given width; polygon fills its points (diagonal edges allowed); band is a path of the given width through its points; fill floods from x,y across the open ground no other zone claims, stopped by other zones and by the box x1..y2 when given. clip decides what shapes keep: "unclaimed" (default) keeps open grass ground that no other zone holds, so zones tile without overlapping, "ground" keeps open grass ground even where other zones lie, "none" keeps every in-map cell. Open ground excludes fixed landmarks. mode "add" or "cut" changes an existing zone's cells instead of replacing them. Explicit cells use integer map coordinates and are kept as given. tag takes a preset; customTag names a facility in the user's language (at most 24 characters) and creates or reuses the map's custom tag. Chips mark a point and require a tag or customTag. Routes are arrows through points, dashed by default. Measurements take two endpoints on one row or column, multiples of 0.5. New zones are numbered in creation order. The result summarizes the annotation instead of echoing its cells. This edits annotation history independently of terrain history.

customTag.description: The text of a custom tag, in the user's language.

size.description: Caption size; none draws a zone with no caption, as paths in a dense plan.

width.description: band: its width in cells; ring: its thickness.

cut.description: Subtract this shape from the shapes before it instead of adding it.

name: remove_annotation
description: Remove one finished planning annotation by its id. Read get_annotations first. Respects the annotation lock and selected region; never removes terrain, objects or an unfinished draft.

name: inspect_region
description: Read a rectangle (max 45x45) as a compact token grid: what an object on each cell stands on. Use this before editing — do not guess current terrain.

name: get_objects
description: List placed objects (id, catalogId, position, rotation, elevation), at most 80 per call. Pass x1,y1,x2,y2 to list only objects placed in that rectangle, and category to list one catalog category.

name: get_selection
description: Get the user's current region selection (bbox + cell count). Call when the user refers to 'here' or 'the selected area'.

name: get_catalog_item
description: Full catalog details for one item id (size, traits, display name, maxCount).

name: view_map
description: See the map as a rendered image (on vision models) or a token grid. Pass x1,y1,x2,y2 to view just that region, close up. Rendered images carry a coordinate ruler so you can map what you see to the cells you edit. Use it to judge COMPOSITION — shapes, balance, ragged edges — after major terrain or decoration work. The map shows what is built in its true colours; layer "plan" adds the planning annotations. layer "ground" shows the terrain alone, one colour per level, water by its level and every waterfall marked: the picture to judge levels, terraces and falls by, which the rendered map shows only as faint shades. Costs tokens on vision models; prefer evaluate_map for objective metrics.

layer.description: map (default): the rendered map as built, true colours. plan: the same with the planning annotations drawn over it. ground: the terrain alone by level.

name: evaluate_map
description: Inspect whole-map design heuristics and trends. These are suggestions, not game rules or task completion criteria: low scores and REGRESSED trends do not require edits outside the user request. A small task needs no scorecard.

name: update_plan
description: Set stages for substantial dependent work or when the user asks for a plan. Use short labels covering only requested outcomes. To report progress on an existing plan, send completedStages alone, the number of consecutive stages already finished. This updates progress without editing the map or running a scorecard. Compact tasks can be built directly.

completedStages.description: Number of consecutive completed stages in the existing plan. Send without stages; verify existing work before marking it complete.

name: list_app_actions
description: List what you can do in the app outside the map: settings, view options, windows, preparing an export, the blueprint and planet libraries, and reading the app's Help and key bindings. Returns each action id with its arguments, its effect (answer, change or outward) and its current value. Call it before run_app_action.

name: run_app_action
description: Run one app action from list_app_actions. Use it only for what the user asked: it changes the app, never the map. An export action opens the export window with the choices set, or the export notice for a blueprint file; the user confirms the download there.

args.description: The action's arguments by name, as list_app_actions gives them.

name: suggest_reply
description: When your closing message leaves ONE obvious next step (a yes/no offer, a single natural follow-up), call this with the short reply the user would most likely send, in the user's own language. It appears as a one-tap suggestion inside their reply box, which shows about 30 characters in a Latin script and about 15 in Chinese, Japanese or Korean and simply cuts off what does not fit — so keep it to a few words. Skip it whenever the next step is genuinely open.

reply.description: The predicted user reply, verbatim-sendable. A few words: ~30 Latin characters, ~15 CJK.

name: paint_terrain
description: Paint mountain or water under the cells of a shape given as flat coordinates: shape "rect" with x1,y1,x2,y2, "circle", or "picture" (rows of text) for any outline, such as a terrace with bays and spurs or a crescent round a pool. The terrain lies under exactly those cells and reaches half a cell past them on every side, so it is centred where the same rectangle of objects would be; the cells touching it rest partly on it, and the result names the nearest clear ones. For a pond on flat grass, paint water at elevation 0 only: surrounding grass contains it; no mountain rim is needed. Mountain auto-builds support tiers 1..elevation (give only the FINAL elevation; mountain elevation 0 clears terrain). Elevated water needs supporting terrain and enclosing banks before this call finishes. Read partial results before continuing.

shape.description: Area form: "rect" fills x1,y1..x2,y2 (inclusive corners); "circle" fills radius r around cx,cy; "line" strokes x1,y1..x2,y2 at width; "cells" reads the cells array; "picture" reads a shape drawn as rows of text from x1,y1.

outline.description: With rect or circle: only the border cells (e.g. a mountain rim to contain water).

picture.description: For shape "picture": the shape drawn as rows of text, top row first, its top-left cell at x1,y1. "#" is a cell of the shape, "." is not. Draw any outline this way: a star, a letter, a crescent, an island with coves. Make the rows mirror images of themselves when the shape should be symmetric. Write a run of one mark as the mark and its count in braces: "#{12}.{4}" is twelve "#" then four ".".

scale.description: For shape "picture": how many cells each character stands for on a side (default 1). At 4 a row of 35 characters spans 140 cells, for outlines at island scale.

zone.description: A planning zone's number (get_annotations): the call keeps to that zone's cells, and to the given area as well when one is given.

elevation.description: The final elevation; the game numbers this layer elevation + 1.

smooth.description: Auto-trim the painted edges (rounded chamfer / 45-degree bevel) — use for natural-looking cliffs and banks.

name: erase_terrain
description: Clear the terrain (mountain/water) under cells back to flat ground; like paint_terrain it reaches half a cell past them on every side.

shape.description: Area form: "rect" fills x1,y1..x2,y2 (inclusive corners); "circle" fills radius r around cx,cy; "line" strokes x1,y1..x2,y2 at width; "cells" reads the cells array; "picture" reads a shape drawn as rows of text from x1,y1.

outline.description: With rect or circle: only the border cells (e.g. a mountain rim to contain water).

picture.description: For shape "picture": the shape drawn as rows of text, top row first, its top-left cell at x1,y1. "#" is a cell of the shape, "." is not. Draw any outline this way: a star, a letter, a crescent, an island with coves. Make the rows mirror images of themselves when the shape should be symmetric. Write a run of one mark as the mark and its count in braces: "#{12}.{4}" is twelve "#" then four ".".

scale.description: For shape "picture": how many cells each character stands for on a side (default 1). At 4 a row of 35 characters spans 140 cells, for outlines at island scale.

name: place_object
description: Place a catalog item with its top-left anchor at (x,y). Ramps snap automatically — aim at a cliff-edge cell. BRIDGES: aim at a GAP cell (water/void, mid-channel) — use the anchors from find_bridge_sites. Returns the final (possibly snapped) placement.

name: remove_object
description: Remove a placed object by its id (from get_objects).

name: rotate_object
description: Rotate an existing rotatable object to an absolute rotation (re-validates placement).

name: trim_corner
description: Cosmetic corner trim on the terrain under cell x,y: corner names which corner of that cell's ground is cut, so the TL corner of a pond painted under x1,y1..x2,y2 is x1,y1 with corner TL and its BR corner is x2,y2 with corner BR. Style 'fan' (rounded), 'tri' (45-degree bevel), 'square' (reset), 'empty' (cut away).

layer.description: What to trim at that cell (default 'terrain').

name: find_flat_areas
description: Search the whole map for flat buildable spots where a footprint of minWidth x minHeight fits (grass zone, uniform elevation, no water, no objects; includes the +1 right/bottom margin the flat trait checks, so place_object at a returned anchor will pass). Pass catalogId (and rotation) to search for that item: its own turned footprint, beach as well where its groundZones allow it, and for a house the level ground its door side needs (V-PLACE-DOOR). Use this instead of guessing where things fit.

minWidth.description: Footprint width; taken from catalogId when given.

minHeight.description: Footprint height; taken from catalogId when given.

catalogId.description: The item to be placed: its footprint, ground zones and door decide the fit.

elevation.description: Terrain elevation to search on (default 0 = flat ground).

limit.description: Max anchors to return (default 5, spread apart).

name: scatter_objects
description: Place many items at once in an ordered pattern over a rectangle. "grid" (the default) plants a lattice on every step-th cell, an orchard or a bed of evenly spaced plants; "fill" covers every cell in row order, a solid bed; "border" lines the rectangle's edge, a hedge or a flower frame around a plot, a pool or a house (around water or a platform painted under x1,y1..x2,y2 the nearest clear border is the rectangle two cells larger on every side, which the paint result names); "checker" takes alternate cells, and two checker calls with offset 0 and 1 weave two species. "scatter" places at random and is for a wild look the user asked for. One species per call reads as one bed; make one call per bed, row or frame with enough count to complete it. Illegal spots are skipped. One undo step. Returns counts and placed anchors.

catalogIds.description: ONE id for an ordered pattern; several are drawn from at random, for scatter only.

rect.description: Scatter area; the flat corners x1,y1,x2,y2 mean the same.

zone.description: A planning zone's number (get_annotations): the call keeps to that zone's cells, and to the given area as well when one is given.

pattern.description: grid = a lattice of every step-th cell (default); fill = every cell; even = columns x rows spread evenly across the rectangle, equal gaps and equal margins; border = the edge of the rectangle; checker = alternate cells; scatter = random.

offset.description: Which half of the checker to take (default 0).

step.description: Grid pitch for pattern "grid" (default 2: an open lattice).

spacing.description: Extra min distance between placed items (default 0; trees already keep their own exclusion radius). Read by pattern "scatter" only.

name: sculpt_terrace
description: Sculpt an organic terraced hill: 1-3 stacked tiers of blob-shaped mountain with rounded edge cuts. Use for irregular hills; paint_terrain can make precise or formal shapes. Same seed = same shape.

seed.description: Shape seed (derived from the site when omitted, so the same call replays).

name: sculpt_wall
description: Raise a banded wall or tall plateau in one call. Bands step up +3 per inset ring, the crest stays flat and pavable, and flood:true sinks a crest pool inside its own rim. Use when the requested scene needs a tall backdrop; sculpt_terrace builds smaller organic hills.

edge.description: Site the wall AS the map's boundary: abutting this edge of the buildable grass, spanning it, depth rows deep (overrides the corners). A backing wall is a boundary condition, not a centerpiece.

depth.description: Rows deep when edge is given (default 14).

crest.description: Crest elevation (default 6; lowered automatically if the rect is too shallow for the insets).

flood.description: Sink a crest pool (water at crest elevation inside its own rim).

smooth.description: round (default) trims the outer cliffs organically; rect keeps them crisp.

name: sink_pool
description: Sink a POOL COURT in one legal stroke: a narrow bench rim (mountain at `elevation`) along the rectangle's edge holding water at the bench's own height — the containment the water rules demand, so it cannot revert half-built. islets:true leaves bench islets inside the water, each holding one object and 4 cells from the next (the parterre grid; the result names the scatter_objects call that plants them). For terraced pool courts; ground-level lakes stay paint_terrain work.

islets.description: Leave the lattice of plantable islets inside the water.

smooth.description: round (default) trims the bench corners; rect keeps them crisp.

name: raise_platform
description: Raise a rectangle of ground x1,y1,x2,y2 to an elevation and place a ramp up to it on one side, in one step: a terrace behind buildings, a platform under a court or pool, a step of a stepped garden. access names the side the ramp goes on (the side the path arrives from); the ramp lands as near the middle of that side as the rules allow. For a platform higher than one layer, raise it one layer at a time, each call a smaller rectangle on the last (at most 3). Objects stand on top on exactly the cells of the rectangle, and the result names the nearest clear cells around it. Build on top with the usual tools; objects take the elevation under them.

elevation.description: The elevation of the top; the ground is 0.

access.description: The side the ramp goes on.

name: copy_area
description: Repeat a finished motif: copy the terrain and objects inside the source rectangle x1,y1,x2,y2 (at most 32 cells a side) to each place in copies, in one step. Build one unit well (a framed bed, a house with its yard, an orchard block, a pool court), then lay it in a row, a grid or mirrored pairs. Each copy gives x,y, the top-left cell its frame lands on. flip "horizontal" mirrors it left to right and "vertical" top to bottom; turns rotates it clockwise by quarter turns after the flip. For left-right symmetry about a vertical axis with the source spanning x1..x2 and the axis lying between columns a and a+1, the mirrored copy has x = 2a + 1 - x2, the same y and flip "horizontal". Copies land on open ground: what already stands at a target is kept, and the result names what each copy could not lay.

copies.description: Where each copy lands, at most 12.

name: replace_objects
description: Replace every object of one catalog id inside the rectangle x1,y1,x2,y2 with another id of the same footprint, each at the same cell and rotation, in one step. Use it after copy_area so that copies of one layout differ in species or colour, or to change the planting of a bed without rebuilding it.

to.description: Catalog id to put in its place.

name: mirror_area
description: Make two sides match: build ONE side of an entrance, a path, a court or a pond, then mirror the rectangle x1,y1,x2,y2 across a line, in one step. The tool computes where the mirror image lands, so the two sides are exactly symmetric, terrain and objects alike. Never build the two sides of something symmetric with separate calls. The other side must be open ground: what already stands there is kept and reported.

axisX.description: A vertical mirror line: a whole number c runs through the middle of column c (a path 1 or 3 wide centred on c); c + 0.5 runs between columns c and c + 1 (a path 2 wide on c and c + 1).

axisY.description: A horizontal mirror line, given the same way for rows.

name: check_build
description: Check what stands in the rectangle x1,y1,x2,y2 for faults a careful builder would fix, found by computation, not by looking: a door with no path, a path cut off or leading nowhere, water left in two pieces, sides meant to match that do not (objects, paving, water and raised ground alike), a row with uneven gaps, planting off-centre on its bed. Each finding names the cells. Call it once when a part is built, before you move on, while a fix is still one step.

name: carve_river
description: Carve a MEANDERING river through waypoints (a smooth curve through every waypoint, constant width, rounded banks): Smart Build's river. It runs downhill from its higher end, drops over a terrace step in a framed waterfall, and opens into a small pool at a dry end. Use 3-5 waypoints with sideways offsets for natural bends; straight 2-point calls are for canals. Banks stay bridgeable where the width is 3-6.

width.description: Channel width (default 4). An even width is centred on the waypoints' cells; an odd one lies half a cell up and left of them.

name: clear_area
description: Make room: in ONE step, remove every (non-locked) object touching the given cells AND erase the terrain under them back to flat grass. Use before reshaping an area instead of removing objects one by one. NEVER answer a refused placement by clearing a district you built — fix the exact cells instead. A clear removing more than 25 objects or covering more than 400 cells refuses unless demolish:true acknowledges the scale.

shape.description: Area form: "rect" fills x1,y1..x2,y2 (inclusive corners); "circle" fills radius r around cx,cy; "line" strokes x1,y1..x2,y2 at width; "cells" reads the cells array; "picture" reads a shape drawn as rows of text from x1,y1.

outline.description: With rect or circle: only the border cells (e.g. a mountain rim to contain water).

picture.description: For shape "picture": the shape drawn as rows of text, top row first, its top-left cell at x1,y1. "#" is a cell of the shape, "." is not. Draw any outline this way: a star, a letter, a crescent, an island with coves. Make the rows mirror images of themselves when the shape should be symmetric. Write a run of one mark as the mark and its count in braces: "#{12}.{4}" is twelve "#" then four ".".

scale.description: For shape "picture": how many cells each character stands for on a side (default 1). At 4 a row of 35 characters spans 140 cells, for outlines at island scale.

demolish.description: Acknowledge a large demolition (over 25 objects or 400 cells).

name: find_speckle
description: Find candidate planting patterns for optional review. Findings are aesthetic heuristics, not errors. Inspect relevant patches before deciding whether a local adjustment serves the request. Intentional mixed planting and small groups can remain; never clear a finding blindly.

name: find_bridge_sites
description: Search for spots where a bridge can legally be placed (a straight gap of water/void/lower ground within the bridge's waterSpan, with flat EQUAL-height banks). Returns anchor cells you can pass directly to place_object. ALWAYS use this before placing a bridge — valid sites are rare and invisible in the token grid.

catalogId.description: Bridge item id (determines deck width); default bridge-plank.

name: find_ramp_sites
description: Scan for validated ramp placements connecting elevation tiers (the ramp equivalent of find_bridge_sites). Returns anchor cells, the catalog ramp item whose heightDrop matches each cliff, and which elevations it connects. Optional nearX/nearY and limit. Use before placing ramps instead of guessing cliff edges.

name: build_road
description: Lay a road in one call: places one road tile per cell along a line given as flat x1,y1,x2,y2 (or explicit cells), skipping illegal cells. End-caps and bends are auto-trimmed like the manual road brush (smooth:"off" keeps them square). One undo step. Use instead of placing road cells one by one.

shape.description: Path form: "line" strokes x1,y1..x2,y2 at width (bare corners mean the same); "cells" reads the cells array.

zone.description: A planning zone's number (get_annotations): the call keeps to that zone's cells, and to the given area as well when one is given.

smooth.description: End-cap/bend trim style (default 'round', the manual brush's Auto Trim).

name: lay_route
description: Lay one path from (x1,y1) to (x2,y2) across whatever lies between, in one step: it climbs each change of level with a stair or ramp, crosses water with a bridge, goes round what stands in the way and meets standing pavement squarely. A point on a building means its door. It connects the two points or lays nothing and says where it stopped. Use it for each stretch of the main route, giving the places it should pass as the ends of successive calls, and for the path to each door, so that every level and every door is reached.

catalogId.description: The paving, a road id from the CATALOG (default: the map's main paving).

name: draw_area
description: Build a whole place from a drawing: rows of text, one character per cell, top-left at (x,y). Built-in marks: "." leaves the cell as it is, "~" water, a digit raised ground at that level (0 is flat ground, 1-9 higher). Every other character is defined in legend, one line each: "T=tree-apple", "p=path-stone", "h=house-id@90" (rotation), and "+" joins ground with things: "t=1+tree-apple" is a tree on level 1, "a=1+path-stone" paving on level 1. Ground is laid first, then paving, then everything else, in one undo step. A thing with no level of its own stands at the level of the ground drawn around it. Ground reaches half a cell past its marks. Whatever stands keeps its ground, so water drawn right beside a thing stops half a cell short of it and the thing stays on dry ground; water between two things needs two "~" across to show. Where two kinds of ground meet, the half cell between them goes to the one drawn less, the figure: a pool in a terrace or a shape of land in a pool keeps its drawn shape. A water body takes the level of the lowest ground around it, so a pool drawn on a terrace lies in the terrace. An item larger than one cell is one mark at its top-left cell, the rest of its footprint left "."; trees and houses need a free cell between them. mirror completes the drawing so both sides match exactly: "x" mirrors it to the right (draw the left half), "y" downward (draw the top half), "xy" both (draw the top-left quarter); give x2,y2, the far corner of the area, and draw the half rounded up: the tool completes it to exactly that size. repeatX and repeatY lay the finished drawing as a tile, gapX and gapY cells apart. scale draws ground at island size: each character stands for a square of that many cells on a side, so 35 characters span 140 cells; a drawing at a scale holds ground marks only, and x2,y2 stay in cells. The result counts what landed per mark and names what was refused.

reads_as.description: Before the rows: what a visitor must see here to call this place what was asked, and where this drawing puts each of it. A court is closed in on its sides, has a floor to stand on and one thing at its centre; an orchard is one tree in rows with lanes between; a word is letters a visitor can read, each one drawn as its letter. For a correction, what it restores.

x2.description: Right column the finished drawing must end on. With mirror "x" or "xy" draw the left half, rounded up: the tool completes it to exactly this width, sharing the middle column when the width is odd.

y2.description: Bottom row the finished drawing must end on; with mirror "y" or "xy" draw the top half, rounded up.

rows.description: The drawing, top row first; every row the same length. Write a run of one mark as the mark and its count in braces: "2{26}3{20}" is twenty-six 2s then twenty 3s.

legend.description: One line per mark you define: "<character>=<catalogId>", optionally "@<rotation>" and "<level>+" or "water+" before it. A mark may also be ground alone: "<character>=<level>" for land, "<character>=water<level>" for water held at that level, such as a pool raised on a terrace inside a ring of the terrace. A drawing does not make falls: unstated water touching lower ground is laid at the lower level, and water at a stated level must be ringed by ground of its own level; carve_river begun inside a raised pool makes the falls.

mirror.description: Complete the drawing by its mirror image: x to the right, y downward, xy both.

seam.description: Only without x2/y2. shared (default): the last column or row drawn is the middle, drawn once, for an odd size. doubled: it is repeated, for an even size.

replace.description: Remove what already stands on the cells that carry a mark before drawing (default false: occupied cells are skipped and reported).

scale.description: Cells each character stands for on a side (default 1). Above 1 the drawing holds ground only: digits, "~", "." and ground marks of the legend.

name: list_skills
description: List the available build playbooks (proven multi-step recipes for villages, hills, rivers…). Cheap — call it when the user asks for a composite scene.

name: load_skill
description: Load a technique or style reference from list_skills when relevant. Apply the parts that help the requested result; examples and optional features do not expand the task. Do not reload an already loaded skill.

name: delegate_task
description: Hand one region of a job of several regions to a helper: a sub-agent with a fresh context that builds on the same map and sees none of this conversation, so the brief must say everything it needs. Build the shared ground and paths yourself first. The helper edits only inside x1,y1..x2,y2 (inclusive corners, cut to the user's region when one is set) and cannot undo. A region of at most 1600 cells with no side over 56 is one place, built by a helper. A larger one, up to 72 on a side, is a district: it goes to a lead of its own, who plans it and briefs helpers for its places. Helpers briefed in the same turn work at the same time, so brief every region that is ready in one turn and give them bounds that do not overlap. The result gives a status (done, partial, capped or failed), how many write calls landed and how many were refused or reverted, what the region gained or lost, and the helper's report. Read it instead of inspecting the region again, and look only where it names a problem.

label.description: Short name shown to the user while the helper works, a few words, e.g. "north grove".

goal.description: The idea of the whole place in a sentence, then what this region is and the one thing that makes it memorable.

include.description: What must be there, one short phrase each.

preserve.description: What must be kept as it is, one short phrase each.

interfaces.description: How the region meets its neighbours: entry cells, the ground level at its edges.

skills.description: Skills the helper loads before it builds.

done.description: Completion checks, one short phrase each.

name: undo
description: Undo the last N edit steps (default 1). Each of your write tool calls is one step.

name: redo
description: Redo the last N undone edit steps (default 1), like the editor Redo button.
